ov: Terrapins are turtles of fresh or brackish water with clawed feet rather than flippers. The name comes from an Algonquian word for the diamondback terrapin, a turtle of salt marshes on the US East and Gulf coasts, named for the diamond pattern on its shell.

why.et: The diamondback was a gourmet delicacy in the early 1900s and was hunted almost to extinction.
why.h: In most of its range it hibernates through the colder months in the mud of creeks and marshes.

rg: Diamondback: US East Coast from Cape Cod to the Florida Keys, the Gulf of Mexico coast and Bermuda.
df: Diamondback: fish, crabs, shrimp, marine snails, clams, mussels, worms, insects and carrion, with a little algae.
fx: Diamondbacks can live in full-strength seawater, using salt glands by their eyes, but they are not true sea turtles.
Diamondbacks live about 25 years in the wild and up to 40 in captivity.
